1.title: Gate of Hell: Rise of Demons v3.0
1.description: An intense action survival game where you must hold back the tides of hell.
1.fullDescription:
A demonic portal has torn open beneath the city, and the spirits climbing out of it erode reality with every step they take. You command the exorcists who hold the line: summon them into **28 deployment slots** across two lanes, promote them through **four tiers**, and keep **Portal Erosion** below 100% while the Depth counter drives you further into the abyss.
      Every kill pays out **Soul Energy**, the currency behind everything you do. Summon an exorcist, promote one into a stronger class, change a unit's job entirely, or spend it on shrines whose auras buff every ally standing near them. Equipment drops across six tiers fill **18 gear slots**, relics stack permanent bonuses run after run, and the bestiary rewards you for cataloguing what you kill.
      **Version 3.0** is the largest content pass since launch: eight new shrines bring the roster to 21, equipment gains tier 5 and 6, a full sound-effect layer ships with volume and mute controls, the interface gains font-size options, and every demon sprite in the game has been redrawn. Above it all the **Gargoyle** wakes as your Depth grows, stacking global debuffs on attack speed, range, damage, and Soul Energy income until only a clean, concentrated defensive line survives.
1.controls: Mouse Click: Attack and select upgrades / Drag: Place defensive structures
1.tips: Promote before you expand. A **tier 3 exorcist** out-damages two tier 1 units for less **Soul Energy**, and summon cost climbs by **5 SE** every time you place a new one. Shrines buff only the allies near them, so build them into your densest cluster rather than the empty lane. Watch the **Gargoyle**: from **Depth 5** onward it debuffs attack speed, range, damage, and SE income globally, and those penalties escalate faster than raw unit count can compensate for. Keep **Portal Erosion** in view — it is the only thing that actually ends your run.
1.lore:
In the year **2099**, a group of scientists attempted to tap into a subterranean energy source, only to discover it was a prison for the oldest entities in the universe.
      The "**Lords of the Pit**" had been trapped for eons, fed only by the echoes of human sorrow. When the drill pierced the final seal, they didn't just walk out—they tore the reality around them.
      The **Old City** was the first to fall, its skyscrapers becoming monuments to despair. But in the shadows, a secret order known as the "**Scribes of the Flame**" had been preparing for this day for centuries.
      They infused modern technology with ancient runes, creating the weapons you now wield. The battle isn't just for territory; it's for the very soul of the planet.
features: 84 Exorcist Types Across 28 Deployment Slots
Four-Tier Promotion Trees and 200 SE Job Changes
21 Aura Shrines — 8 New in v3.0
Six Equipment Tiers Across 18 Gear Slots
54 Demons in 5 Families with a Boss Every 10 Stages
Stackable Relics and a Bestiary That Pays Out
Full SFX, Volume, Font Size, and Language Settings
Web & Mobile Friendly
1.objectives: Hold back endless demon waves, strategically upgrade towers and weapons with **Soul Fragments**, and survive long enough to close the Gate of Hell before **Elite Demons** overwhelm your defenses.

faq.q: How do I start the first wave?
faq.a: Place at least one defensive tower near the chokepoint, then confirm your placement to begin the first demon wave. The game paces itself — you have a brief setup window before enemies spawn.

faq.q: What are Soul Fragments used for?
faq.a: Soul Fragments are the main currency, earned by defeating demons. Spend them on tower upgrades, new weapon research, and the Aegis-7 orbital strike. Don't spend all of them at once — keep a reserve for emergencies.

faq.q: When do Elite Demons appear?
faq.a: Elite Demons begin appearing around Wave 10. They are significantly tougher than standard enemies, so save orbital strikes specifically for these encounters rather than burning them on regular waves.

faq.q: What is the best early strategy?
faq.a: Upgrade fire rate on your starting tower before spending on additional structures. A fast single tower at the main chokepoint outperforms two slow towers spread across the map in the early waves.

faq.q: Is there an end to the game?
faq.a: The wave count is effectively infinite with increasing difficulty. Your goal is to survive as long as possible and maximize your survival time for the global leaderboard.

2.title: Galaxy Launch: Infinite Fleet
2.description: An addictive clicker game where you expand your fleet and conquer the galaxy.
2.fullDescription:
Create a new fleet at the edge of the vast universe and become the ruler of the galaxy. Galaxy Launch starts with simple clicks but offers deep strategic management as your empire grows.
      Extract resources from planets and research cutting-edge technology to enhance your ships' firepower. Watching hundreds of ships fly through space in real-time is a unique thrill found only in clicker games.
      Test your limits in infinite space, upgrade your space station, and venture into further galaxies. The peace—or conquest—of the galaxy is entirely in your hands.
      As the **Grand Admiral** of the **Neo-Terran Hegemony**, you are tasked with the **Great Expansion**. Your starting point is the "**Vanguard Station**," a derelict refinery on the edge of the **Andromeda Galaxy**.
      You must optimize the ship-to-resource ratio, balancing the production of mining drones with heavy interceptors. The galaxy is not empty; pirate factions and rogue AI swarms will attempt to intercept your cargo.
      Unlock the "**Dyson Swarm**" project to harness the full power of nearby stars, allowing for the construction of **Dreadnought-class** vessels that can dominate entire star systems.
2.controls: Left Click: Collect resources / Menu Buttons: Buy upgrades and ships
2.tips: Automate your resource collection as soon as possible. Researching "**Hyper-drive**" early will significantly boost your expansion speed. Don't forget to upgrade your **Station shields**, as the pirate raids become much more frequent after you conquer your **third planet**.
2.lore:
The year is **4022**. Earth is a distant memory, a myth shared by travelers in the deep void. Humanity now lives in the "**Flotilla**," a massive collection of interconnected ships wandering the stars.
      But resources are dwindling, and the internal factions are on the brink of civil war. Your mission, sanctioned by the **Elder Council**, is to find the "**Primal Star**"—a legendary sun that never dies.
      To reach it, you must navigate through the **Great Barrier**, a region of space filled with ancient debris and gravitational anomalies. You are the last hope for a civilization that has forgotten how to call a planet "home".
features: Infinite Incremental Gameplay Loop
Over 50 Unique Ship Types to Unlock
Deep Technology Research Tree
Dynamic Pirate Raid Events
Prestige System: "Galaxy Jump" for Permanent Multipliers
Visual Upgrades for your Space Station
Web & Mobile Friendly
2.objectives: Expand your fleet from a single derelict station at the galaxy's edge, automate resource collection, defeat pirate raids, and advance toward the legendary **Primal Star** before the **Flotilla**'s factions collapse.

faq.q: How do I get started?
faq.a: Click the resource node to begin generating fleet fuel manually. Use your first earnings to buy an automated mining drone so you can step away without losing progress.

faq.q: What is the 'Galaxy Jump' prestige system?
faq.a: Galaxy Jump resets your current run in exchange for permanent multipliers that carry forward. Triggering it at the right moment — typically after conquering your third or fourth planet — compounds your total earnings far faster than continuing the same run.

faq.q: How do I survive pirate raids?
faq.a: Pirate raids ramp up significantly after you claim your third planet. Upgrade your Station shields before expanding further, and maintain a reserve of interceptors so raids don't drain your resource stockpile mid-expansion.

faq.q: What does Hyper-drive do?
faq.a: Researching Hyper-drive dramatically increases fleet travel speed between planets, shortening the time between resource drops and enabling faster colonization — it's one of the highest-value early research picks.

faq.q: Is there an endpoint to the game?
faq.a: The stated goal is finding the Primal Star beyond the Great Barrier, but the gameplay loop is effectively infinite. Each Galaxy Jump cycle lets you push deeper into the universe while your permanent multipliers grow.

3.title: Idle Avatar RPG
3.description: Develop your own avatar and explore a mysterious world that grows automatically.
3.fullDescription:
The best choice for those who want the fun of growth even in a busy daily life: Idle Avatar RPG. Even while you sleep, your avatar fights monsters, acquires precious items, and grows stronger.
      Combine various classes and skill trees to create your own unique hero. Hundreds of equipment sets and gem enhancement systems provide endless nurturing fun.
      Mysterious dungeon exploration, boss raids, and a ranking system to compete with players worldwide! Experience the comfort of an idle game and the depth of an RPG simultaneously.
      Enter the realm of **Aethelgard**, a world where thought shapes reality. You play as a **Soul-Binder**, a rare individual capable of projecting their consciousness into powerful Avatars.
      Your physical body remains in the **Temple of Stasis**, but your Avatar roams the **Wildlands**, battling the **Shadow-Blight** that threatens to consume the world's remaining light.
      Gather "**Echo Dust**" from defeated foes to attune your Avatar to the elements—Fire, Ice, and Void. The deeper you venture into the Wildlands, the more complex the loot becomes, requiring you to master the art of **Enchanting**.
3.controls: Auto-battle supported / Click: Manual skill use and equipment management
3.tips: Keep an eye on the "**Rebirth**" mechanic. Resetting your progress at the right time provides massive permanent bonuses. Prioritize the "**Luck**" stat early on to increase the drop rate of **Rare-tier** equipment from low-level goblins.
3.lore:
**Aethelgard** was once a unified paradise, governed by the "**Great Weavers**" who spun the threads of fate. But a catastrophic event known as the "**Unraveling**" broke the loom, scattering the threads across the void.
      Now, the world exists as fragmented islands of reality, held together only by the will of the Soul-Binders. The **Shadow-Blight** is the manifestation of the void's hunger to erase what remains.
      Every piece of equipment you find is a relic from the old world, a solidified memory of a civilization that was once perfect. By wearing them, you are literally wearing history itself.
features: True Offline Progress: Gains while App is Closed
Complex Class Tree with over 20 Specializations
Rune-based Skill Customization
Global Raid Bosses with Massive Rewards
Player-driven Economy and Trading
Pet System: Tame Monsters to Fight Alongside You
3.objectives: Project your Avatar into the **Wildlands** of **Aethelgard**, gather **Echo Dust** from defeated monsters, equip relics of the old world, and grow powerful enough through **Rebirth** cycles to push back the **Shadow-Blight** threatening to erase all remaining light.

controlsTable.action: Avatar fights continuously without input

faq.q: Do I need to keep the game open to progress?
faq.a: No — the game features true offline progress. Your Avatar continues fighting and collecting while the app is closed, so you can log back in after hours and collect accumulated rewards.

faq.q: When should I use the Rebirth mechanic?
faq.a: Rebirth at the point where your Avatar's progress begins to slow significantly. The permanent bonuses from a well-timed Rebirth snowball across all future runs, accelerating your growth far more than grinding the same stage.

faq.q: What stat should I prioritize first?
faq.a: Prioritize Luck early on. Higher Luck increases the drop rate of Rare-tier equipment from even low-level enemies, which sets up a much stronger foundation for mid-game class specialization.

faq.q: What is Echo Dust?
faq.a: Echo Dust is the primary attunement resource dropped by defeated foes in the Wildlands. It is used to align your Avatar to one of three elements — Fire, Ice, or Void — and unlocks access to elemental skill branches.

faq.q: What are the relics I collect?
faq.a: Relics are equipment pieces that are literally solidified memories from Aethelgard's destroyed civilization. Wearing them grants stat bonuses and they can be enhanced with the Enchanting system to scale into the late game.

5.title: GEM MERGE
5.description: Drop gems into a physics vessel, merge matching cuts into rarer jewels, and chain combos to forge the Legendary gem.
5.fullDescription:
GEM MERGE is a physics merge puzzle with **eleven distinct gem cuts**. Aim, drop, and let gravity do the rest: when two gems of the same level touch they fuse into the next cut, from the humble **Trilliant** up to the **Legendary gem**.
      Speed is rewarded. Land another merge within **1.3 seconds** and the combo counter climbs, and each combo step upgrades your next gem, so a **x3 combo** hands you a **Lv.3** gem instead of a Lv.1. Skill, not luck, decides what falls next.
      **Two Lv.10 gems** forge a Legendary gem. It triggers a cinematic, clears itself off the board, and is stored forever in your **Vault**. The **Gem Catalog** tracks every cut you have spawned and earned across all your runs.
      Every merge has its own pop, combos play a rising melody, and the Legendary forge gets a fanfare. Play in English, Korean, or Japanese.
5.controls: Mouse: move to aim, click to drop. Touch: drag to aim, release to drop.
5.tips: Keep big gems low and small gems high. Merge fast: a second merge inside **1.3s** starts a combo, and **combo x2, x3, x4** upgrades your next gem to that level. A gem that settles above the **danger line** ends the run, so never let a stack idle near the top.
5.lore:
The **Crystal Caves** hold treasures beyond imagination. Only those with the sharpest minds can master the art of gem resonance.
      Long ago, the Great **Gem-Smiths** used these gems to power the floating cities of **Sky-Reach**. But when the cities fell, the knowledge was lost, and the gems scattered.
      Now, you are the first seeker to find the **Alchemist's Vessel**, the only container capable of stabilizing the raw power of merged gems.
      Each cut represents a stage of celestial evolution, from the simple **Trilliant** to the **Legendary gem** that the Gem-Smiths sealed away in their vaults.
features: Eleven unique gem cuts, each with its own shape and color
Real 2D physics: gems bounce, roll, and settle
Combo system: fast merges upgrade your next gem (up to Lv.4)
Score streak tiers with screen shake and shifting ambience
Legendary gem cinematic and a persistent Vault
Gem Catalog with lifetime spawn and merge tracking
Per-level merge sounds, combo melody, and Legendary fanfare
English, Korean, and Japanese
Web & Mobile Friendly
5.objectives: Drop and merge same-level gems inside the **Alchemist's Vessel**, keep the stack below the **danger line**, and chain combos to forge a **Legendary gem** for your **Vault**.

Drop the gem

Toggle sound
Open the Gem Catalog
Switch language

faq.q: How does merging work?
faq.a: When two gems of the same level touch, they fuse into the next cut and the new gem pops upward slightly. If it lands on another gem of its new level, it merges again, so chains happen naturally.

faq.q: How do combos work?
faq.a: Merge again within 1.3 seconds to raise the combo counter. Combo x2 makes your next gem Lv.2, x3 makes it Lv.3, and x4 makes it Lv.4, the cap. The upgrade never downgrades until you drop it, so you can take a moment to aim.

faq.q: What ends the run?
faq.a: The run ends when a gem comes to rest above the danger line near the top of the vessel. A gem that is still bouncing past the line does not count, so a tall stack can survive as long as it keeps moving.

faq.q: What happens when I make a Legendary gem?
faq.a: Merging two Lv.10 gems forges a Legendary gem worth 200 points. It plays a short cinematic, leaves the board so it never blocks you, and is added to your Vault permanently.

faq.q: What does the Gem Catalog show?
faq.a: The catalog lists all eleven cuts with how many times each has spawned and how many you have earned through merges, across every run on this device.

6.title: Trade Tycoon - Civilization
6.description: Build your empire, trade resources, and lead your civilization to prosperity.
6.fullDescription:
Experience the thrill of building a civilization from the ground up in Trade Tycoon. Manage resources, establish trade routes, and make strategic decisions to expand your influence across the globe.
      This game is currently in production, bringing deep economic simulation and city-building elements to your browser. Stay tuned for more updates!
      In the dawn of the **Bronze Age**, you are the leader of a small coastal tribe. Your journey begins with simple barter, but your ambition is to create a **Silk Road** that spans continents.
      You must manage the "**Happiness-Tax**" balance, ensuring your citizens are productive while keeping the treasury full for military expansion.
      The world is a living marketplace; prices of **gold, spices, and iron** fluctuate based on global supply and demand. Will you be a peaceful merchant prince or a ruthless conqueror who controls the world's resources through force?
6.controls: Mouse: Navigate menus and manage city structures.
6.tips: Balance your production and consumption. **Over-expansion** can lead to a resource crisis. Always keep a surplus of "**Grain**" for the **winter months**, as production drops and prices skyrocket during the off-season.
6.lore:
From humble beginnings to a global superpower. Your dynasty will be remembered for centuries to come.
      The legends tell of the "**First Merchant**," who traded a single pearl for a ship, and that ship for a kingdom. 
      But history is written by the victors. In this world, the gods only smile upon those who can provide the finest offerings of **silk and wine**.
      Your civilization's rise is written in the ledgers of time, where every coin earned is a brick in your eternal monument.
features: Deep Economic Market Simulation
Multiple Tech Eras from Bronze to Space
Complex Diplomacy and War Mechanics
Procedural World Maps with Unique Resources
Customizable City Layouts for Optimized Production
Leaderboard for the Wealthiest Empires
6.objectives: Grow your coastal tribe from **Bronze Age** barter into a globe-spanning empire by establishing profitable trade routes, managing resource surpluses, and out-competing rival civilizations on the **wealth leaderboard**.

controlsTable.action: Select city structures and open upgrade menus
Assign resources to production or trade routes
Initiate trade agreements or military actions
Advance through technology eras

faq.q: What resources matter most early on?
faq.a: Grain is the most critical early resource — production drops in winter while prices spike, so always keep a healthy surplus before expanding. Neglecting Grain leads to starvation penalties that cripple your economy.

faq.q: How do I balance expansion without crashing?
faq.a: Over-expansion is the most common mistake. Expand only when your current territories are generating stable surplus, and check the Happiness-Tax balance before adding new cities to avoid productivity penalties.

faq.q: How do market prices work?
faq.a: Prices for gold, spices, and iron fluctuate based on global supply and demand. Watch the market panel and sell high-demand goods rather than hoarding them, then reinvest in production of currently scarce commodities.

faq.q: What is the difference between peaceful and military play?
faq.a: Peaceful merchant strategies compound wealth faster in the mid-game through compounding trade routes. Military conquest gives faster map control but incurs maintenance costs and risks counter-attacks that can destabilize your treasury.

faq.q: What is the end goal?
faq.a: The leaderboard ranks the wealthiest empires, so your target is maximum accumulated wealth. Reaching the Space era via the technology tree unlocks the highest-value production buildings in the game.

7.title: 15s Click Challenge
7.description: Tap the glowing target before 15 seconds run out. Chain combos, clear the level, climb the checkpoints.
7.fullDescription:
15s Click Challenge gives you exactly **15 seconds** per round. A glowing target jumps around the playfield — every hit is +1, every miss costs you half a second off the clock. Reach the level's **click quota** before the timer hits zero to clear it and move up a level.
      The target does not wait for you. It relocates on its own every second at level 1 and gets **7% faster** every level, bottoming out at a jump every **0.3 seconds**. It also shrinks every five levels, and from level 11 on every jump crosses at least **40% of the playfield**.
      Chain hits within **1.5 seconds** to build a combo. **Six combo tiers** ramp up the pitch of the hit sound, the particle bursts, the spark lines and the camera punch — one miss and the combo is gone.
      Fail a round and you drop back to the last **checkpoint** (levels 1, 6, 11, 16...), so pushing deep is always a gamble. In the last 5 seconds the ball fades and the remaining seconds are drawn inside it.

8.title: OMOK
8.description: A masterpiece of strategy and intuition. Master the ancient art of Five-in-a-Row.
8.fullDescription:
Experience the timeless elegance of Omok, the classic abstract strategy board game known worldwide as **Gomoku**. Simple to learn but offering infinite strategic depth, Omok challenges you to align **five stones in a row**—horizontally, vertically, or diagonally—before your opponent does.
      Every move is a delicate balance between offense and defense. Will you build your own unstoppable sequence, or will you focus on anticipating and blocking your rival's every turn? 
      Whether you are a casual player looking for a quick mental workout or a strategy enthusiast seeking a true competitive challenge, Omok provides a pure, minimalist gaming experience that tests the limits of your foresight and tactical skill.
      Play against a **sophisticated AI** calibrated to the styles of legendary masters. Every game is a lesson in patience and geometric vision.

8.lore:
A game of **kings and scholars**. The black and white stones represent the harmony and conflict of the universe.
      The origin of Omok is lost to time, but some say it was played by the gods to decide the boundaries of the stars. 
      The board itself is a **map of the soul**, where every stone represents a decision, and the lines represent the paths we choose to follow.
      To win is not just to align **five stones**, but to demonstrate a superior understanding of the balance between creation and destruction.

faq.q: How do I win a game of OMOK?
faq.a: Place five of your stones in a continuous row in any direction — horizontal, vertical, or diagonal — before your opponent does. The first to achieve five-in-a-row wins the round.

faq.q: What is an 'Open Three'?
faq.a: An Open Three is a sequence of three of your stones with both ends unblocked. It is a powerful formation because it threatens to become an Open Four, which is nearly impossible to stop. Building Open Threes while blocking your opponent's is a core mid-game strategy.

faq.q: What is an Open Four and why is it critical?
faq.a: An Open Four is four stones in a row with at least one open end. If your opponent has one, you must block it immediately — failing to do so on that very turn means they win the next move.

faq.q: Why is controlling the center important?
faq.a: Stones placed near the center have more directions available to form rows of five. Corner and edge stones are restricted to fewer angles, making them easier for an opponent to preemptively block.

faq.q: How advanced is the AI?
faq.a: The AI is calibrated to styles of legendary masters. It reads Open Threes and Open Fours accurately at higher difficulties. Playing against it at medium difficulty is an effective way to learn to recognize patterns before competing against humans.

9.title: 40th Century: Void Survivor
9.description: Survive in the void of the 40th century. Battle cosmic horrors and collect ancient artifacts.

Step into the desolate **40th century** where humanity fights for survival in the vast emptiness of the void. 40th Century: Void Survivor is an intense action-survival game that challenges your reflexes and strategic thinking.
      Navigate through waves of cosmic horrors, upgrading your ship and abilities as you progress. Collect mysterious artifacts and antiques that grant powerful bonuses and reveal the history of a lost civilization.
      The further you go, the more dangerous the void becomes. Can you reach the final stage and become the ultimate survivor?
      You are the pilot of the "**Void-Walker**," a craft capable of dipping in and out of the lightless dimension. Your fuel is the very essence of the horrors you destroy.
      The game utilizes a "**Quantum Upgrade**" system, where every level-up presents you with **three random paths** to power. Will you focus on kinetic projectiles or esoteric energy beams?

9.lore:
The stars have gone dark. In the silence of the **40th century**, the Void whispers. Only the bravest can hear the path to salvation.
      The "**Solar Extinction**" was not a natural event; it was a harvest. The entities from the Void returned to claim what they planted billions of years ago.
      Humanity's last cities are built on the hulls of dead suns, protected only by the thinning layers of reality. You are a scavenger of the void, searching for the "**Omega Code**," the only thing capable of rebooting the universe.

faq.q: What is the Quantum Upgrade system?

10.title: Kingdom of Ashes - Endless War
10.description: Macro-scale faction war for the ruins of Alea — direct the Golden Army or the Infernal Legion across an endless wave-survival simulation.
10.fullDescription:
Kingdom of Ashes - Endless War is the strategy entry in the Kingdom of Ashes series. After the **Dicefall** shattered Alea, two surviving orders rose from the ash and turned the ruined kingdom into a permanent battlefield. You are an **Arbiter** — neither side claims you, both sides answer to you — and your job is to keep the war from ending.
      You do not command individual soldiers. You set the divine laws, tactical formations, and deployment cadence for entire legions. Wave after wave, the **Golden Army** of the surviving spires and the **Infernal Legion** of the ash-pits trade ground across the **Threshold**, a malleable plane where every prayer and every sin takes physical form as a warrior.
      Combat runs as a continuous simulation. You pick your starting roster, set the **Karma** balance between the two factions, react to dynamic battlefield events, and adjust formations as the enemy composition shifts. Wave depth, battles won, and Karma swings all feed the persistent global war progress tracker.
      Three pressure points define every run: the Karma meter (centered unlocks the **Divine Storm** screen-clear), the ranged/melee balance (a **40/60 split** is the floor, not the ceiling), and timing your surges around **Solar Flares** and **Abyssal Rifts**. Master those three and the wave count climbs. Ignore any one and the ash takes you.

10.tips: Diversify your army — a mix of ranged and melee is essential against the evolving wave compositions. Keep the **Karma** meter centered to retain the **Divine Storm** screen-clear; over-committing to one faction locks you out of it. Read incoming wave composition before the wave hits — adjusting on the fly is where the game lives. Time your unit surges with **Solar Flares** and **Abyssal Rifts** to compound their event buffs.
10.lore:
The **Dicefall** ended Alea as a realm. It did not end the war for it.
      Two orders survived the shattering. The **Golden Army** gathered in the last unburned spires and took the dawn for their banner. The **Infernal Legion** crawled out of the ash-pits beneath the broken cities and claimed the night. Between them lies the **Threshold** — a plane that bends to belief, where every prayer and every sin from the old world surfaces as a warrior with a sword in its hand.
      You are the **Arbiter**. You did not choose this title; the Dicefall did, the same way it chose the dice-bonded survivors in the rest of Alea. Your purpose is not to win the war for either side. Your purpose is to keep it going — because the moment one faction takes the Threshold, the ash falls everywhere, and what little remains of Alea finally goes silent.

faq.q: What is the Karma meter?
faq.a: Karma tracks your balance between directing souls to the Golden Army versus the Infernal Legion. Keeping it centered unlocks the Divine Storm ability, which clears an entire screen of enemies and is one of the strongest tools the Arbiter has.

faq.q: What army composition works best?

faq.q: What are Abyssal Rifts and Solar Flares?

11.title: Kingdom of Ashes - Dice War
11.description: Roll five dice into a poker hand, field the squad it summons, and fight turn-based grid battles through endless chapters of monsters.
11.fullDescription:
Kingdom of Ashes - Dice War is a turn-based tactics roguelike where your army comes from a poker hand. Each stage opens with a roll of five coloured dice, and the hand you make — High Card up to Five of a Kind — decides which allies spawn, from a pair of Warriors up to the **Greek Hero**. Keep the dice you like and reroll the rest (one reroll by default, more with upgrades), pay 2 Gold for a **Risk Reroll** that throws all five again, or Re-color to reshuffle colours while keeping your pattern. When the dice that form your hand share a colour the whole squad gets that **colour bonus**: Red trades HP for ATK, Green adds HP and range, Blue adds movement, Purple stretches range at the cost of HP, Gold is a balanced boost.
Battles play out on a 16×12 grid split into three zones. **Enemy territory** cuts ally stats to a fifth and drains 5 HP a turn, the neutral middle spawns **special tiles** — attack and range buffs, heal tiles, water that slows and blocks shots, lava that burns, pyramids that wall off lines of fire, one-shot invincibility — and enemies who push into your side fight at double strength. Tap a unit to see its move range, tap a red-outlined enemy to strike; anything that survives a hit **counters** for 30% of its ATK, so ranged units and positioning matter more than raw numbers.
Every chapter is ten stages, several with multiple waves and reinforcements, against ten monster types that each bring a mechanic: Goblin Scouts dodge, Orc Warriors enrage under half HP, Skeleton Archers block the first hit, Dark Knights lifesteal, Gargoyles shrug off 2 damage, Liches revive once, Stone Golems knock you back, Dragon Lings splash, Slimes split, and the **Void Horror** absorbs damage, phase-shifts and spreads fear. Surviving allies level up between stages (+20% HP, +15% ATK, full heal) and carry their HP forward. Clearing a stage earns Meta Points and, every second stage, a Monster Head; a chapter clear pays out Monster Cores and rolls straight into the next, harder chapter.
Progress persists two ways. Monster Heads and Cores unlock a 70-node **Passive Tree** across four phases — pick two of four paths in Phase I, one of three in Phase II, two of four in Phase III, then the final node — with branches like Attack, Defense, Agility, Survival, Inferno and Phantom. Meta Points buy seven permanent **Meta Upgrades**: Iron Body, Sharpened Blade, Tactical Reform (extra rerolls), Flame Resist, Color Amplify, Supplies and Elite Training. The **Dungeon** screen maps every chapter's ten stages — cleared, next up, or still locked — with the enemy roster of each stage you have reached, a six-step tutorial covers dice, zones, movement, counters, waves and upgrades, and the game plays in English, Korean and Japanese.
11.controls: Tap or click a unit: select it and show its blue move range / Tap a blue tile: move there / Tap a red-outlined enemy: attack it / Tap a die: keep it for the next Reroll / Re-color: reshuffle colours without changing your hand / Risk Reroll: spend 2 Gold to reroll all five dice / Mouse hover: preview any unit or tile in the Unit Info panel / Top bar icons: Passive Tree, Hand Reference, Start Battle / Battle log: mouse wheel or drag to scroll history
11.tips: A **Full House** (Shieldmaiden, Sniper, Priest) is the most reliable squad — tank in front, sniper behind, healer keeping both alive. Match colours before chasing a bigger hand: **Green** (HP +8, range +1) on two Warriors outlasts a colourless Four of a Kind. Never end a turn in **enemy territory** — your stats drop to a fifth and you bleed 5 HP every turn. Let enemies come to your side instead; they fight at ×2 there but you keep full stats and the heal and range tiles are usually closer to you. **Counters** hit for 30% of ATK, so open with the Sniper or Archer from outside enemy range and let melee finish. Save a **Risk Reroll** for a Straight-or-better fishing turn when you have Gold to spare — 2 Gold is cheap compared to fighting a boss stage with two Warriors. Step on **Invincible** tiles the turn before a Dragon Ling or Void Horror reaches you. Buy **Tactical Reform** first on the Meta screen: an extra reroll every stage is worth more than any flat stat.
11.lore:
The Kingdom of Ashes fell long ago, and what was left of its armies fell with it. All that remains is the **Dice of Ash** — five relics that answer only to chance. Roll them on the burned stones of the old war grounds and the dead take shape again: warriors, archers, shield-bearers, priests, and if the dice align, a hero out of the oldest legends.
But the monsters that ended the kingdom never left. Slimes seep from the meadows, goblins raid the roads, the crypts spill out skeletons and liches, and deeper still something without a name is waking in the void. Every chapter you clear only pushes the darkness back one step. The war goes on.

faq.q: How do poker hands decide my army?
faq.a: The five dice are scored like poker. High Card spawns two Warriors, One Pair a Shieldmaiden and Warrior, Two Pair an Assassin and Priest, Three of a Kind a Berserker and Warrior, a Straight a Sniper, Archer and Warrior, a Full House Shieldmaiden, Sniper and Priest, Four of a Kind Berserker, Assassin, Sniper and Warrior, and Five of a Kind the Greek Hero with a Priest.

faq.q: What do the dice colours do?
faq.a: If the dice that make your hand share a colour (all of them for hands of one or two dice, at least three otherwise), every spawned unit gets that bonus: Red ATK +3 / HP −2, Green HP +8 / range +1, Blue MOV +2 / ATK −1, Purple range +2 / HP −2, Gold ATK +2 / HP +4. Mixed colours give nothing.

faq.q: Why are my units so weak on the left side of the grid?
faq.a: Columns 0–3 are enemy territory: ally stats are multiplied by 0.2 and each unit loses 5 HP per turn there. Columns 12–15 are your side, where enemies fight at double strength instead. The neutral middle is where the special tiles spawn.

faq.q: What happens when I lose?
faq.a: The run ends and you go to the Meta screen. Meta Points earned that run (+2 per stage, +5 per chapter) stay with you, as do Monster Heads, Cores and every Passive Tree node and Meta Upgrade you bought. The next run starts at Chapter 1 Stage 1 with all of it active.

faq.q: Do my units carry over between stages?
faq.a: Yes. Every surviving ally levels up when the stage is cleared — +20% max HP, +15% ATK and a full heal — and keeps its HP into the next stage. New dice rolls add to the squad rather than replacing it, so protecting veterans is how you snowball.

faq.q: Is there an ending?
faq.a: Clearing Chapter 1 shows a victory screen, then the war continues. Chapters are endless and enemies scale up each time, with bigger Monster Core payouts from Chapter 5 and Chapter 8 onward.

12.title: Heroes of the Last Nexus
12.description: A strategic hero collection RPG where you must gather heroes to defend the Last Nexus.
12.fullDescription: In a dying world, the **Last Nexus** is all that remains. You are a **Soul-Binder** tasked with summoning legendary heroes to protect this final bastion against the encroaching darkness. Gather your team, level up your heroes, and face waves of monsters in this epic strategic adventure.
12.controls: Mouse/Touch: Summon heroes and manage your team.
12.tips: Focus on upgrading your **tank heroes** early. Don't forget to use your **Soul-Binder** abilities to support your team when things get tough. **Synergies** between different classes are the key to surviving later waves.
12.lore: The **Last Nexus** was created by the **Ancient Celestials** to hold back the **Void**. For eons, it stood as a beacon of light, but its power is fading. Only the gathering of the **Heroes of Legend** can restore its strength and push back the darkness once and for all.
features: Over 50 Unique Heroes to Collect
Strategic Team Formations and Synergies
Epic Boss Battles and Infinite Monster Waves
Deep Hero Progression and Skill Trees
Global Leaderboard for Most Heroes Collected
Web & Mobile Friendly
12.objectives: Summon legendary heroes to defend the **Last Nexus** from endless monster waves, level up your roster, and collect as many heroes as possible to restore the Nexus's fading power before the **Void** consumes it.

Select and manage hero upgrades
Activate Soul-Binder support abilities

faq.q: How do I get started?
faq.a: Summon your first hero using available resources and place them to intercept the incoming monster wave. The game explains summoning order through its tutorial — focus on a tank hero first to soak early damage.

faq.q: Which heroes should I upgrade first?
faq.a: Tank heroes should be upgraded first. They absorb incoming damage and keep your fragile damage-dealers alive long enough to output meaningful DPS. A low-tier tank with several upgrades outperforms a high-tier caster who dies quickly.

faq.q: What are hero synergies?
faq.a: Different hero classes interact with each other — combining tank, support, and damage-dealer classes unlocks passive bonuses that none could achieve alone. Experimenting with compositions is key to surviving later waves.

faq.q: What are Soul-Binder abilities?
faq.a: As the Soul-Binder, you have your own set of support abilities separate from the heroes. Use them when your frontline is overwhelmed rather than saving them indefinitely — they exist precisely for high-pressure moments.

faq.q: What is the win condition?
faq.a: There is no finite end — the wave count is endless and the Void grows stronger continuously. Your score on the global leaderboard reflects the number of unique heroes collected, so breadth of collection matters as much as survival depth.

13.title: Timing Chef
13.description: Master the art of perfect timing in the kitchen!
13.fullDescription:
Step into the shoes of an aspiring chef where precision is everything. In Timing Chef, your goal is to cook various dishes to perfection by hitting the **sweet spot**. 
      Manage multiple orders, watch your **heat levels**, and serve up culinary masterpieces to hungry customers. 
      As you progress, unlock new recipes and upgrade your kitchen equipment to handle the **dinner rush**. Can you earn the elusive **five-star rating** and become the ultimate Timing Chef?
13.controls: Mouse/Touch: Click or tap to start and stop cooking actions.
13.tips: Pay close attention to the **visual and audio cues**. Each ingredient has its own **'perfect' window**. Don't let the heat build up too much, or you'll **burn the dish**!
13.lore:
In the high-stakes world of competitive cooking, a single second can be the difference between a **Michelin star** and a kitchen disaster. 
      The legendary 'Timing Chef' was said to be able to hear the exact moment a steak reached **medium-rare** from across the room. 
      Do you have the senses and the nerves to follow in their footsteps?
features: Precision-based Rhythm Cooking Gameplay
Variety of Unlockable Recipes and Cuisines
Kitchen Upgrade System for Faster Cooking
Challenging 'Rush Hour' Mode
Aesthetic Pixel Art and Satisfying Sound Effects
Web & Mobile Friendly
13.objectives: Cook every dish to perfection by clicking at precisely the right moment, manage incoming orders without letting heat overflow, and earn a **five-star rating** by completing the **dinner rush** flawlessly.

controlsTable.action: Start a cooking action
Stop cooking at the exact perfect window

faq.q: How do I cook a dish perfectly?
faq.a: Each ingredient has a visual and audio 'perfect' window — watch the heat indicator and listen for the cue, then click to stop cooking at that exact moment. Clicking too early or too late drops the dish quality.

faq.q: What happens if heat builds up too much?
faq.a: Excess heat burns the dish, failing the order entirely. Monitor your heat gauge continuously and click to stop cooking before it enters the red zone — it is better to undercook slightly than to burn.

faq.q: How do I handle multiple orders at once?
faq.a: Prioritize orders with the shortest remaining time on their countdown. Quick-completing one dish frees your attention for the next, rather than juggling all simultaneously and risking multiple burns.

faq.q: What do kitchen upgrades do?
faq.a: Upgrades reduce cooking time, widen the 'perfect' window, or add capacity for additional simultaneous orders. Investing in wider perfect windows is the most forgiving upgrade for players still learning ingredient timings.

faq.q: What is Rush Hour mode?
faq.a: Rush Hour is a high-intensity mode that floods the kitchen with orders faster than normal play. It tests whether you can maintain precision timing under extreme time pressure — it's the ultimate challenge for five-star players.

featuredComments.name: PerfectWindow
featuredComments.text: Listen before you look. The audio cue for the perfect window is slightly ahead of the visual indicator, which gives you a fraction of a second of extra reaction time once you train your ear to it.

featuredComments.name: FiveStarRush
featuredComments.text: Rush Hour mode is unforgiving in the best way. Normal play gives you time to think. Rush Hour takes that away and you find out very quickly which recipes you actually have memorized.

featuredComments.name: HeatPanic
featuredComments.text: The heat gauge creeping into the red while you're mid-click on a second dish is a specific kind of stress I was not prepared for on my first run. Now I check heat before starting any new action.

featuredComments.name: MichelinDash
featuredComments.text: Wider perfect window upgrades are absolutely the right call early. They're not glamorous but they let you build confidence and internalize ingredient timings before the margins get tight.

featuredComments.name: SizzleTimer
featuredComments.text: Prioritize the countdown order, not the one that looks most urgent. Lowest remaining time wins every time even if another dish looks more done. Manage by timer, not by eye.

14.title: Fruit Frenzy v1.3
14.description: A fast vertical catcher: slide the basket under falling fruit, dodge bombs or shoot them out of the sky, and ride combos through seven levels.
14.fullDescription:
Fruit Frenzy is a vertical arcade catcher built for one-handed phone play and just as sharp on desktop. Slide the **basket** left and right to catch fruit as it falls; every catch is 1 point, and once your **combo** reaches 3 every catch is worth 2. Rare stars pay 3. Miss a fruit or catch a **bomb** and you lose one of your **3 lives** — lose all three and the run is over.
      Score carries you through **seven levels** (Novice to Myth): fruit falls faster, spawns thicker, bombs get more common and the basket shrinks. From level 2 fruit starts pulling **moves** — hopping off an invisible floor, braking mid-air, skidding sideways, and from level 3 hovering before a plunge — while bombs begin to **seek** the basket.
      v1.3 adds a **gun**: click or tap to fire a bullet straight up. Shooting a bomb detonates it mid-air for a point; shooting a fruit destroys it and costs a life. You bank 2 bullets and one reloads every ~1.5 seconds. A very rare **ammo crate** drifts down now and then — catch it to grow the bank (up to 4) and refill on the spot. **50 achievements** track fruit caught, bombs avoided, combo streaks, score milestones and level clears.
14.controls: Mouse / Touch: move the basket. On PC the mouse locks to the canvas while playing (Esc releases it). Left-click or tap: fire a bullet straight up. Bullets pop bombs for a point but destroy fruit for a life, so aim only at bombs.
14.tips: Combo is the whole economy — once it hits **3**, every fruit pays double, so a clean streak out-scores any risky grab. Shoot **bombs**, never fruit: a shot bomb is **+1** and counts as avoided, a shot fruit is **−1 life**. Keep one bullet banked for **seeking bombs** — they lean toward the basket from level 2 and are far easier to pop than to dodge. Hovering fruit **spins up** before it plunges; that spin is your cue to get underneath. A miss counts the instant the fruit clears the basket's underside, so commit early instead of chasing. The **ammo crate** (slow, cyan glow) costs nothing to miss but grows your bank to 4 — always worth the detour.
14.lore:
The **Orchard of Abundance** is a grove suspended between seasons, where every fruit ever grown still ripens somewhere on its impossible trees. Lately the harvest has turned mischievous: fruit hops, brakes and hovers on the way down, and something is rolling bombs off the branches.
      You are the newest **Harvester**, basket in one hand and a sling of bullets in the other. Catch what falls, shoot what explodes, and keep the orchard's rhythm alive as long as your three lives last.

Fire a bullet straight up from the basket
Release the mouse lock on PC

faq.q: How does scoring work?
faq.a: Each fruit is 1 point, or 2 once your combo reaches 3. Rare stars are worth 3, and shooting a bomb is also 1 point. Missing a fruit, catching a bomb, or shooting a fruit costs one of your 3 lives.

faq.q: How do I level up?
faq.a: Levels advance on score: 10, 25, 45, 70, 100 and 140 points take you from Novice up to Myth. Each level speeds up the fall, thickens spawns, raises the bomb chance and shrinks the basket a little.

faq.q: How does shooting work?
faq.a: Click or tap to fire straight up. You bank 2 bullets and one reloads every ~1.5 seconds — the ammo pips top-left show the state. Hitting a bomb detonates it for +1; hitting a fruit destroys it and costs a life, so only shoot at bombs.

faq.q: What is the ammo crate?
faq.a: A very rare, slow-drifting crate with a cyan glow. Catching it grows your bullet bank by one (up to 4) and refills it. Missing it costs nothing, and bullets pass straight through it.

faq.q: Why do fruit and bombs move strangely at higher levels?
faq.a: From level 2 fruit can hop off an invisible floor, brake in the air or skid sideways, and bombs can steer toward the basket. From level 3 fruit can hover before plunging, and from level 4 bombs hover too. Hovering objects spin up before they drop — that is your tell.

15.title: Kingdom of Ashes - Colosseum
15.description: An auto-battler roguelike in the Kingdom of Ashes series — draft from 105 heroes across 8 elements, merge them to 5★, and hold a 3×3 arena for 7 rounds a stage against an enemy that drafts back.
15.fullDescription:
Kingdom of Ashes - Colosseum is the auto-battler entry in the Kingdom of Ashes series (formerly Kingdom's Last Stand). You never swing a sword yourself: between rounds you spend gold in the shop, drag heroes onto a **3×3 grid**, then watch both sides fight it out on their own. Every stage is **7 rounds** — win 4 and you advance, pick one of three permanent rewards and take an artifact; win all 7 and take two.
      The roster is **105 heroes** across **8 elements** — Fire, Frost, Lightning, Nature, Holy, Dark, Physical and Arcane — costing 2 to 8 gold, each with its own skill and a cinematic cut-in when it fires. Placement is decided by range: the front column for tanks and melee, mid for supports and assassins, back for ranged damage and healers. Buy a copy of a hero you already own, drop it on the original, and it stars up; a cost-6+ hero that reaches ★3 **evolves** and at ★5 **ascends**, bolting a second effect onto its skill.
      Elements do two jobs. Affinity is a four-way cycle — Fire beats Nature beats Lightning beats Frost beats Fire — at ±30%, Holy and Dark hurt each other both ways, Physical shrugs off elemental damage and Arcane cuts through it. Synergy counts copies: two heroes of one element light Tier I, three Tier II, five Tier III, and a full mono-element grid of nine Tier IV. Fire stacks attack and burn, Frost armour and slows, Lightning speed and crits, Nature regen, Holy shields, Dark attack per kill, Physical armour pierce, Arcane cooldowns and skill damage.
      Around the fights sits the roguelike layer: a **bench**, a **sacrifice** altar that turns a spare hero into permanent column stats, a Kingdom tab of six permanent upgrades, **33 artifacts**, eleven stage rewards from interest caps to Elemental Harmony, and an achievement wall with tiered titles. Fights that drag past turn 12 hit **enrage** — attack climbs every turn, healing and armour halve at 16 — so stalling lineups lose to fast ones. The enemy drafts against what you fielded, so the stage-25 arena is nothing like the stage-3 one. Plays in English, Korean and Japanese.
15.controls: Drag: place a hero from the shop, move it, or drop it on a copy to merge / Tap or hover a hero: stats, skill, lore / Shop: Buy, Sell, Reroll, Lock / Battle Start: run the round / Speed: 1x, 1.75x, 2x
15.tips: Read the range before you buy: range 1 goes front, 2 mid, 3 back, and a hero can't be dropped into the wrong column. Chase one element to three copies early — **Tier II synergy** is where the bonuses start paying for the gold. Merges need all nine grid slots filled and cap at two per round, so bench the spare copy instead of selling it. Kill gold and interest are small change; the round supply funds you, so never skip a round. When the enrage warning shows at turn 10, healing and armour are on a timer — finishers beat sustain.
15.lore:
**Alea** settled its arguments by the roll of the dice until the **Dicefall** burned it to ash. What the fire left standing was the **Colosseum** — the one thing the old kingdom built too well to fall — and the ash-lords who hold it have made it the last court in the land. No more dice. Every claim is settled by nine champions on a marked floor.
      You arrive with a purse and no army. The heroes who answer your gold are the leftovers of a dead kingdom — frost knights whose fortresses melted, inquisitors with no church, golems that outlived their makers — and they do not care whose banner they stand under. Each stage the ash-lords send a heavier roster, drafted against whatever you fielded last.
      Win four rounds of seven and the arena admits you to the next tier. Lose, and your champions go back to the sand with everyone else. Rumour holds there is a floor beneath the arena where the last dice still roll. Nobody has fought deep enough to see it.

faq.q: Is this the same game as Kingdom's Last Stand?
faq.a: Yes — same auto-battler, renamed and folded into the Kingdom of Ashes series. The 2026 update added Japanese, an enemy AI that drafts against your elements, the bench and evolution systems, a full balance pass (SPD is now an action rate, the DEF curve was reworked, synergy bonuses that the text promised now actually fire) and a performance pass. Your personal best on this page carries over.

faq.q: How does a stage work?
faq.a: Seven rounds. Each round you shop, arrange, and fight one auto-battle. Four wins advance you to the next stage with a reward pick and an artifact; seven of seven pays two artifacts and bonus score. Fewer than four means the stage failed — you can retry it, but that ends the scored run.

faq.q: How do I merge, and what is evolution?
faq.a: Buy a second copy of a hero and drop it on the first: ★1 becomes ★2 and so on up to ★5, raising HP, ATK and DEF each step. Merging needs all nine grid slots filled and is capped at two per round. Heroes costing 6 or more evolve at ★3 and ascend at ★5, which adds a second effect to their skill — the Dragon's breath sets every enemy on fire, Judgment Bolt gains an AoE wave.

faq.q: Which elements counter which?
faq.a: Fire beats Nature, Nature beats Lightning, Lightning beats Frost, Frost beats Fire — +30% one way, −30% the other. Holy and Dark deal +30% to each other. Physical takes 15% less from elemental attacks; Arcane deals 15% more to elemental targets. Physical against Arcane is neutral.

faq.q: What triggers enrage?
faq.a: Turn 10 warns, turn 12 starts it: every unit on the field gains attack each turn. At turn 16 the ramp steepens, healing drops by half and all DEF is halved. It exists so two healer lines can't stall forever — build to end fights before it, or bring the Eternal Hourglass artifact, which stretches the 20-turn battle limit to 30.

faq.q: Does the game save my run?
faq.a: A run is played in one sitting; the game keeps only your language and tutorial state between visits. Your score and highest stage post to your ArcadeDeck personal best after every stage clear and when the run ends.

16.title: Triangle Battle!
16.description: Hot-seat triangle land-grab for 2-6 players on one device: connect pegs, close triangles, and use the +2 bonus and timeout penalty to outscore everyone.
16.fullDescription:
Triangle Battle! is a local multiplayer board game for **2 to 6 players** sharing **one device** — phone, tablet or desktop. The board is a random scatter of pegs; players take turns tapping two pegs to draw a line between them. Close a triangle and it's yours: **+1 point and an extra turn**. Close one whose three sides are all your own color and it's worth **+2**. A triangle with a peg trapped inside doesn't count, and lines can never cross.
      Every turn runs on a **10 or 20 second clock**. Let it expire and the next player is handed a **free random line** — so hesitation actively feeds your opponent. The game ends when no legal line remains; the most points wins.
      A built-in **How to Play** guide opens on first launch, the HUD mirrors for face-to-face phone play, and the whole thing is a lightweight installable PWA with an EN / KO toggle.
16.controls: Tap or click a peg, then a second peg to draw a line between them. Tap the selected peg again to deselect. Drag empty space to pan the board; the minimap shows where you are. Hot-seat turns for 2-6 players on one device. Press ? for the in-game guide. No keyboard needed.
16.tips: Never leave a triangle **two sides of your color** open — the +2 bonus goes to whoever closes it, not whoever started it. Use the **extra turn** from a closed triangle to immediately close a second one. Don't stall on the clock: a timeout hands your opponent a free line. Fewer pegs (10) makes a sharper, faster game; 25 pegs turns it into a long war of blocking.
16.lore:
In the neon-lit arenas of the **Grid**, geometric warriors compete for supremacy. The ancient **Triangle Protocol** demands that only those who can form the perfect shape will ascend.
      Each match is a test of speed, strategy, and spatial mastery. The Grid remembers every triangle ever formed, and the greatest players are immortalized in its luminous halls.

faq.q: How do I score?
faq.a: Closing any triangle is +1 point and gives you another turn. If all three sides of the closed triangle are your own color it is worth +2. A triangle with another peg inside its area does not count.

faq.q: What happens when the timer runs out?
faq.a: The next player receives a free random line and the turn passes to them. There is no unlimited option — pick 10 or 20 seconds in setup.

faq.q: Which lines are illegal?
faq.a: A line cannot cross an existing line, cannot pass over a peg, and cannot duplicate a connection that already exists. The board flashes a warning and the turn continues.

faq.q: How many players can play?
faq.a: 2 to 6 on a single device, hot-seat style. On phones the HUD, timer bar and minimap mirror so a player sitting opposite can read them.

faq.q: When does the game end?
faq.a: When no legal line can be drawn anywhere on the board. The result screen ranks every player by points and shows lines drawn and triangles closed.

17.title: Tank Battle: 1v1
17.description: An intense same-screen 1v1 tank duel built for couch rivalries — destructible cover, ricochet shots, no luck involved.
17.fullDescription:
Tank Battle: 1v1 is a fast-paced couch-multiplayer arena game designed for **two players sharing the same keyboard**. There is no online matchmaking, no account, no waiting room — pull up a friend, pick a side, and start firing. Each round resets in seconds so a single sitting easily turns into thirty matches.
      Maps mix solid walls, **destructible crates**, and **ricochet pads**. Crates absorb one shot and then collapse, shifting cover lines mid-round so static defenders die. **Ricochet pads** bounce projectiles at fixed angles, enabling bank shots around corners — a core skill for higher-level play. Tanks have a brief **reload window** between shots, which means winning a round is usually about controlling your opponent's reload timer, not raw aim.
      Three arena layouts ship with the game (**Symmetric Wedge, Open Plains, Maze**) and unlock as you progress. **Win streaks** build a small momentum bonus that grants slightly faster reload — the only catch-up mechanic in an otherwise pure-skill game. Strategy is everything: rush the opponent before they set up cover, or stake out a sightline and punish their reload? Read your friend, not the screen.
17.controls: Player 1: WASD to move, Space to fire. Player 2: Arrow Keys to move, Enter to fire. Best on a keyboard with N-key rollover — membrane keyboards drop simultaneous inputs and cause lost shots.
17.tips: Never sit still during the enemy's reload — the **catch-up reload bonus** rewards aggression, not entrenchment. Use **destructible crates** as one-shot decoys: fire a probe round into a crate to break cover the opponent was leaning on. **Ricochet pads** beat direct shots on the Maze layout because corridors funnel return fire. On membrane keyboards, choose **Player 1 (WASD)** — Arrow Keys are more likely to ghost on simultaneous-press inputs. Most experienced players win by controlling **map center**, not by sniping from the edges.
17.lore:
The **Tank Arena** is the proving ground of the last age of armor — a sealed crucible where two commanders fight not for territory but for legend. Above the arena, every duel is broadcast to the cities that no longer remember why the war began.
      Every shot counts. Every move is recorded. Only one tank leaves the dust under its own power, and only one name is written into the **iron ledger**.

faq.q: How do rounds work?

faq.q: What are ricochet pads and how do I use them?
faq.a: Ricochet pads bounce projectiles at fixed angles, enabling bank shots around corners. On the Maze layout especially, bounced shots beat direct fire because corridors funnel opponents into predictable positions — practicing fixed-angle bank shots is a high-return skill.

faq.q: How do destructible crates affect strategy?
faq.a: Crates absorb exactly one shot and then collapse, eliminating that cover. Fire a probe shot into a crate your opponent is leaning on to remove their protection mid-round. Static defenders relying on crates are particularly vulnerable to this.

faq.q: What is the key to winning firefights?
faq.a: Control your opponent's reload timer. Never sit still during their reload — aggression during that window prevents them from setting up advantageous angles. Most rounds are decided by who exploits the reload gap better, not who aims best.

faq.q: Does keyboard type matter?
faq.a: Yes — N-key rollover keyboards register all simultaneous inputs. Membrane keyboards may drop inputs when both players press simultaneously, which causes missed shots. If you can choose, take Player 1 (WASD) on a membrane board, as Arrow Keys ghost more easily.

18.title: Skyfall
18.description: Free-movement arcade dodge: read the telegraphs, thread meteors, pillars, cracks and homing seekers, bank close-call combos, and grab rare orb drops for the longest run.
18.fullDescription:
Skyfall is a top-down survival arcade game about staying alive under a sky that wants you dead. You steer a tiny pilot anywhere on the ground — no lanes, no jump — and every hazard **shows you where it will land before it does**. Meteors paint a danger disc with a ring that closes onto it at impact; pillars mark their footprint with a dashed ring before shooting up as solid walls you have to slide around; ground cracks glow before they turn lethal. Read the telegraph, move early, live.
      Hazards **unlock by level** (one level every 12 seconds): meteors from the start, **pillars rise** at level 2, **ground cracks** at level 3, and at level 8 **seekers hunt** — homing orbs that spawn at a screen edge, lock on for 5 seconds, and can only be juked, never outfought. Each hazard ramps from its own unlock with hard caps, so the pressure keeps building without ever becoming a wall.
      Scoring rewards nerve, not just time. Surviving pays 100 points a second, and every meteor that explodes **just beside** you is a **CLOSE CALL** that pumps a decaying combo multiplier on top of a base multiplier that grows the longer you last. Every 30 seconds the game pauses and offers a choice of three **Starshards** — run-scoped upgrades such as SWIFT (+10% speed), FORESIGHT (longer warnings), SLIM (smaller hitbox), or DARING (close calls worth +50%). Finished hazards occasionally leave an **orb drop** behind: Shield, Speed, Score x2, Ghost, or Nova — grab it before it blinks out.
      Rendered at a crisp 2x 480x270 with a PICO-8 palette, fully procedural visuals and audio, and a touch layout that works anywhere on the screen. Your best score is saved locally and counts toward your ArcadeDeck personal best.
18.controls: Desktop: move the mouse — your pilot chases the pointer — or use WASD / arrow keys. Mobile: touch anywhere on the screen and drag; a virtual joystick appears under your thumb, lift to stop. Landscape only on phones. Every 30 seconds click or tap one of three Starshard cards to pick an upgrade.
18.tips: Watch the **rings, not the rocks** — a meteor is only lethal at the instant its ring lands on the danger disc, so step out of the disc and step back in for a free **CLOSE CALL**. Keep the combo alive: close calls decay, so string them together in the mid-game when meteors are frequent but still slow. **Pillars are cover** against nothing — seekers ignore them — but they are walls for you, so never let one spawn between you and open ground. When **SEEKERS HUNT** at level 8, run in wide arcs; the orb is slower than you and burns out after 5 seconds. Take **FORESIGHT** or **SLIM** early and **DARING** once you are comfortable brushing meteors. An orb blinks for its last 1.2 seconds — if it is far and blinking, let it go.
18.lore:
The cities below the storm were warned that the sky was falling. They did not believe it until the first crater. Now the storm is permanent, the ground splits and heaves, the towers rise and fall on their own, and something in the debris has learned to **hunt**.
      Only the **dancers** remain — the few who learned to read the sky's warnings and step between catastrophes. Out here, every second is a small refusal to be crushed, and the starshards falling with the rocks are the only gift the storm ever gives.

faq.q: How do I know where a meteor will hit?
faq.a: Every meteor paints a danger disc on the ground with a ring that shrinks onto it; the meteor is lethal only for the instant the ring lands. Leave the disc before that moment — or hover just outside its edge for a close call.

faq.q: What is a CLOSE CALL and why does it matter?
faq.a: A meteor that explodes right next to you without touching you. Each one adds +0.25 to a combo multiplier (capped at 1.5) that decays over time, on top of a base multiplier that grows +0.1 every 15 seconds. Late-game combos are where big scores come from.

faq.q: When do the other hazards appear?
faq.a: Levels tick every 12 seconds. Meteors fall from level 1, pillars rise from level 2, ground cracks open from level 3, and seekers start hunting at level 8. Each hazard ramps from its own unlock and hits a hard cap, so the curve stays fair.

faq.q: How do I deal with seekers?
faq.a: Seekers are homing orbs that spawn at a screen edge, lock on after a short spawn-in, and chase you for 5 seconds. They move slower than you and pass straight through pillars, so run in wide arcs and let them burn out — never corner yourself.

faq.q: What are Starshards?
faq.a: Every 30 seconds the run pauses and you pick one of three upgrades that last for the rest of the run: SWIFT (+10% speed), FORESIGHT (+0.12 s warning), SLIM (smaller hitbox), DARING (close calls worth +50%), PRISMATIC and ECHO (mixed bonuses). Nothing carries between runs.

faq.q: What do the orb drops do?
faq.a: A finished hazard has a small chance to leave an orb that lasts 4 seconds. Shield absorbs one hit, Speed gives ×1.5 movement for 2 s, Score x2 doubles time score for 5 s, Ghost makes you invulnerable for 3 s, and Nova bursts every hazard on screen. Active orbs show in the HUD with a draining ring.

faq.q: Does it work on phones?
faq.a: Yes — rotate to landscape, then touch anywhere and drag. The game pauses while the phone is held in portrait, and the play area respects the notch and home bar.

Spirit Duel is a deep tactical battle game where players **summon powerful spirits** and outmaneuver their opponent through careful **resource management** and strategic decision-making.

Ancient spirits have long walked the boundary between worlds, each one a force of nature given form. In the sacred dueling grounds, two **spirit binders** face off, their wills clashing through the spirits they command.

faq.q: How do I start a duel?
faq.a: Select your roster of spirits before the match begins. In local play, both players take turns on the same device. Against the AI, you play first and alternate turns until one spirit binder's forces are exhausted.

faq.q: What makes resource tempo important?
faq.a: Overextending early — summoning too many spirits at once — leaves you resource-starved in later turns. Pacing your summons to match the opponent's pace prevents being caught unable to respond to their key plays.

faq.q: How do I beat the AI?
faq.a: Watch the AI's summoning patterns across several turns to identify which spirit types it prioritizes. Once you recognize its pattern, you can counter-summon the spirit type that specifically exploits its weakness.

faq.q: Do spirit abilities matter more than their stats?
faq.a: Distinct abilities are what differentiate spirits — stats alone rarely decide duels. Learn each spirit's ability before committing to your roster, and build a team whose abilities cover each other's weaknesses.

faq.q: Is the game better with two players or solo?
faq.a: Both modes are viable. Local 1v1 adds psychological reads and bluffing, which can't be replicated against the AI. Solo play against the AI is the best way to learn ability interactions before competing against friends.

20.title: Polygon Invasion TD
20.description: Geometric tower defense: eight polygon towers, 24 evolutions, 29 corrupted shapes and a Core that only survives 20 leaks.
20.fullDescription:
Polygon Invasion TD is a wave-survival tower defense on a single neon path. Corrupted polygons march from the portal toward your **Core**; you drop towers beside the path, spend the **shards** every kill pays out, and push each tower to **LV3**. Waves get denser and faster every round, a **boss** arrives every fifth wave, and the run ends the moment 20 enemies leak through the gate.
      Your arsenal is eight shapes with eight jobs — the Line fires an instant beam, the Square crushes ground swarms with splash but cannot touch air, the Pentagon is anti-air only, the Hexagon sprays, the Septagon snipes from long range, the Octagon chains three targets and the Nonagon buffs everything in its aura. Every boss kill drops an **EVO core**; spend one on a LV3 tower to pick one of three **evolutions** — 24 in total, from Siege Howitzer and Storm Crown to Wrath Aura.
      The enemy roster grows as you go: 29 corruption types tagged **AIR, SHIELD, GHOST, HEAL, SPLIT, TANK, FAST** and **BOSS**, each logged in the in-game Corruption Logs the first time it appears. Auto-save lets you continue a run later, and your rank at game over — F to S — is decided purely by the peak wave you reached.
20.controls: Mouse / Touch: click or drag to place towers; keys 2–9 pick a shape, Q upgrades, E sells, R evolves, ESC pauses
20.tips: Build a **Square** at the first bend before wave 2 — ground swarms die to splash before they spread. Have one **Pentagon** covering the path by wave 3, when Sky Bishops start flying over your ground towers. Upgrade to **LV3** before buying a fourth tower, and hold every **EVO core** for the shape you have the most of.
20.lore:
The **Polygon Dimension** did not invade with armies. It leaked — one corrupted triangle at a time, through a gate that should never have opened. Every shape that reaches the Core rewrites a little more of the world into its own geometry.
      Your towers are the last clean shapes left. Build, upgrade, evolve and hold the gate. Every wave repelled is a fragment of reality that stays ours.

faq.q: Which tower should I build first?
faq.a: A Square at the first corner. Its splash hits every ground enemy within 80 units, which is exactly what the wave 1–2 swarms of Frail Pawns and Broken Squares need. Follow it with a Triangle or Hexagon for single targets, and add a Pentagon by wave 3 — the Square cannot hit air.

faq.q: What are EVO cores and how do I evolve?
faq.a: Every boss (waves 5, 10, 15 …) drops one EVO core. Select a LV3 tower, press R or tap EVOLVE, and choose one of three evolutions for that shape — the Square, for example, becomes Siege Howitzer (long-range artillery), Pyroclasm (burning splash) or Quake Hammer (slowing splash). An evolution is permanent for that tower.

faq.q: What do the enemy tags mean?
faq.a: AIR flies over ground-only towers (the Square cannot hit it; the Pentagon hits only it). SHIELD carries a shield worth 50% of its health that absorbs damage first — Quill Stinger pierces it. GHOST fades in and out but can be hit the whole time; Phantom Lance deals ×1.5 to it. HEAL restores nearby enemies. SPLIT bursts into Swarm Seeds on death, so kill it inside splash range. TANK is slow and heavy; FAST is the opposite.

faq.q: How does the run end and how is my score decided?
faq.a: Every enemy that reaches the gate costs one Core point and adds corruption (5 for NORMAL, 10 for SPECIAL, 15 for BOSS). At 20 leaks the Core falls. Your score is the peak wave reached; the game-over rank is F below wave 10, then D, C, B and A every five waves, and S at wave 30.

faq.q: Does the Nonagon aura stack?
faq.a: Not with itself — two Nonagons covering the same tower apply only the strongest aura, so spread them over different clusters. The three Nonagon evolutions (Wrath ×4 damage, Tempo ×2.6 fire rate, Empower a mix of both) count as different types and do stack with each other.

faq.q: Can I stop and come back later?
faq.a: Yes. The run auto-saves on every build, upgrade, sell, evolve and wave start; pick CONTINUE on the title screen. The save is cleared when the Core falls.

21.title: Just Jump
21.description: A pure, one-button platformer — time your leaps, stick tricky landings, and push every run further than the last.
21.fullDescription:
Just Jump strips the platformer down to its purest form: jump, land, repeat. There is **one input**. There is one goal. There is one score. Time each leap perfectly to clear gaps, stick tricky landings, and ride the rhythm further than the previous attempt.
      Platforms scroll continuously upward and the gap pattern shifts **every ten platforms** — long stretches reward held inputs, short stretches reward tapping, and mixed stretches punish either rhythm if you commit too early. **Edge landings** count for a small **style bonus** on the score, so the optimal play is always to land as close to the leading edge as you can dare. The further you climb, the faster the world scrolls — eventually **faster than human reaction time**, which is the point.
      Easy to pick up, brutally hard to master. One mistimed jump and the run ends, but the next attempt is **one tap away**. Chase a personal best, then chase the global top of the leaderboard.
21.controls: Click, Tap, or Spacebar to jump. Hold for a longer arc; tap for a short hop. There is no second button, no boost, no shield, no second chance — the entire skill ceiling lives inside the length of one press.
21.tips: Read the rhythm before reacting — most deaths come from over-jumping the first platform of a new pattern. **Short hops** cover more horizontal ground than they feel like they should; trust the physics. Keep your eyes **one platform ahead** of your feet, not on the platform you are leaving. **Edge landings** score a **style bonus** and also leave a longer next-jump window — the safest landing is also usually the highest-scoring one. When the world starts scrolling faster than you can think, switch from reacting to **predicting**: commit to the rhythm, not the visuals.
21.lore:
**No story**. No cutscenes. No upgrades. Just you, a platform, and the **next jump**.
      Every leap is a small **bet against gravity**. How long can you keep winning?

faq.q: What is the difference between a hold and a tap?
faq.a: Holding the input produces a longer, higher arc that clears wider gaps. Tapping produces a short hop for narrow gaps. The entire skill ceiling of the game lives inside knowing when to hold and when to tap.

faq.q: Why do I keep dying at pattern transitions?
faq.a: The gap pattern shifts every ten platforms — long stretches reward held inputs, short stretches reward tapping. Deaths most commonly occur on the first platform of a new pattern because players carry the previous rhythm into the wrong gap size. Read the new pattern before reacting.

faq.q: What is an edge landing?
faq.a: Landing as close to the leading edge of a platform as possible awards a style bonus on top of your score. Edge landings also leave a longer jump window for the next leap, making them both higher-scoring and tactically safer.

faq.q: Where should I look — at my feet or ahead?
faq.a: Keep your eyes one platform ahead of where you are standing, not on the platform you are leaving. Looking at your current position causes late jumps; looking ahead lets you commit to the right input before landing.

faq.q: What do I do when the scrolling gets impossibly fast?
faq.a: Switch from reacting to predicting. At extreme scroll speeds, the gap pattern is the only usable signal. Commit to the platform rhythm rather than tracking individual visuals — trust the physics and let your muscle memory drive the timing.

featuredComments.name: RhythmLeap

featuredComments.name: AheadOfFeet

22.title: Mythic Defender: Heroes Returns v2.0

Mythic Defender: Heroes Returns fuses classic **tower defense with deck-building** strategy. Draw heroes from your **card pool**, place them along the path, and unleash devastating abilities to crush waves of orcs, demons, and worse.

faq.q: How does the card summoning system work?
faq.a: You draw hero cards from your deck at the start of each round. Drag cards onto valid tiles along the enemy path to summon them. Heroes remain on the map until they are defeated or the round ends.

faq.q: Where should I place melee heroes?
faq.a: Front-load tanky melee heroes near chokepoints to absorb damage while ranged casters work safely from the back row. A melee hero positioned deep into the map near your core provides no damage reduction for the path before it.

faq.q: When should I save mana instead of spending it?
faq.a: Save mana for each wave's elite enemies and boss arrivals. Burning all mana on standard enemies leaves you defenseless when the boss appears — bosses require concentrated upgraded firepower, not distributed low-tier units.

faq.q: Is it better to upgrade one hero or place more?
faq.a: Upgrades scale better than placing additional low-tier units. Concentrate your mana on your strongest frontline hero rather than spreading upgrades evenly — a single well-upgraded hero outperforms three under-upgraded ones.

faq.q: What is the Burning Horde?
faq.a: The Burning Horde is the army that has torn through the ancient seals and set citadels ablaze. It consists of orcs, demons, and worse — each wave is a new portion of the Horde pressing toward your position.
